paper_metadata.title: Influence of alloying elements on precipitation formation and mechanical properties of Al – Cr – Mo-Sc-Zr alloys during laser powder bed fusion at room and elevated temperatures
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: Influence of alloying elements on precipitation formation and mechanical properties of Al – Cr – Mo-Sc-Zr alloys during laser powder bed fusion at room and elevated temperatures
High-temperature properties, especially creep results of Al – Cr alloys and Scalmalloy ® (Al – Mg – Mn-Sc-Zr) are presented for the first time

evidence.quote: Three different powders were used in this work: Scalmalloy ® (in the following denoted as ‘MG ’ ), Scancromal ® with a high alloying element content (‘CR-high ’ ), and low alloying content (‘CR-low ’ ).

evidence.quote: The equiaxed dendrites were identified as phases rich in Cr and Mo via EDS measurements.
While CR-low shows the columnar grains and strong epitaxial growth across the melt pools as expected from literature
CR-high is showing still epitaxial growth but much smaller columnar grains and even some fine-grained areas on melt pool boundaries

some bigger equiaxed dendrites of about 1 μ m on the melt pool boundaries (darker regions, higher magnification in Fig. 4 c,g). The equiaxed dendrites were identified as phases rich in Cr and Mo via EDS measurements.

attributes.morphology: elongated in CR-high, compact in CR-low

evidence.quote: At high magnifications (BSE images), small precipitates ( < 1 μ m) become visible on the edges of the columnar grains alongside with a darker contour of the grains. These precipitates coarsen when aged and appear elongated in CR-high ( Fig. 4 d) and compact in CR-low ( Fig. 4 h).
Especially XY-samples, but also Z-samples, show intergranular fracture along the columnar grains as well ( Fig. 6 a,c).

Uniaxial creep tests were carried out at stress values between 49.5 MPa and 222.6 MPa, which were chosen to get creep rates in the range of 10 - 9 – 10 - 4 1/s. The shortest creep test was for CR-high at 222.6 MPa stress with a duration of 0.7 h whereas the test with the longest test duration was 315.3 h for CR-low at 148.7 MPa.
